This is a bit of a lengthy read. I wanted to AskVoat, see what opinions I would get, and just to share this sad story of a proud man, and how his life turned out. This has to do with a neighbor and her family when I grew up. It was the 70's, a great time to be a kid, and I had my best friend. We were both around 5 years old when we met. Were friends for years. Her family had everything you could ever want. Would go up to their cottage every summer, it was awesome. It wasn't just a cottage, it was more like a second home, it had its own library. Beautiful place, even as a kid I loved that place. I'll call her Mary. Her dad was a lawyer, he was in the political circle here in town. There is a picture of him standing next to former President Ford. He's met Reagan. Hunts, Fish, a real go getter. Very respectable man.

Mary has a brother named Joe. Both Mary and Joe were adopted. Joe was always a bit weird, even my oldest sisters when they would sometimes babysit the two, would mention what a weird and troubled kid Joe was. Being around him always made me uneasy. I never truly liked the guy. But being that young, I couldn't understand why, and nothing ever happened, thank god.

We get older, go off to college, I move out of state, we lost touch. I never forgot Mary. I ended up moving back home a couple of years ago. I was at Costco one day, I see this elderly gentleman walking towards me. I squint my eyes as I look at him. Could it be Mr. Reynolds? I haven't seen him in roughly 40 years??? I approached him, and asked if he was Mr.Reynold. Yes it was him. It was Mary's dad! I told him my name, he was absolutely delighted to see me. We talked for a bit, I gave him my number, if Mary wants to call me, give her my number. Couldn't believe my eyes.

She did call me, we caught up on the phone, it was great to talk to her. Her dad is now 91, he's still very sharp, drives, bit scary yeah. Then she got to her brother, who died in Jail, and was a sex offender. I couldn't believe it. All of it makes sense now. Her parents wouldn't tell her he was in jail for the longest time. Ashamed? They were a proud family. Joe made it difficult and hell for them. They tried their best with Joe, it was never enough. I told Mary if her dad ever needed anything, let me know, she lives in Virginia, out of state. She reached out again later, and said her dad needed help with his phone. My husband can help with that. Mary did warn me about Joes wife that lives with her two kids in Mr.Reynolds house, the house she grew up in. The ghetto moved in, along with the drugs.

We went over to visit, I wasn't looking forward to it, but its Mr.Reynolds. I've driven by the house in the past, and it looks run down. The kicker, its in a affluent neighborhood, sticks out like a sore thumb. Its sad to see. We go up to the front door, knock, Mr.Reynold answers with a smile. The smell, the look of the place, my childhood shattered in an instant walking through that door. I spent many years in that once gorgeous house as a kid. Its now run down, crap every where. He almost trips. The walls are banged up. It was so sad to see, and it broke my heart. Met his grandson, he was alright. He's in the 6th grade. He showed me his bedroom, apologized for it being messy, it wasn't just messy, it was squalor. It was disgusting. Mr. Reynolds did mention he doesn't have the patience for the drugs. Mary says she has tried to get help, he has to want it. She's contacted the help for the aging here in town. He's cognitive state, he doesn't qualify for some help. I wish she was his power of attorney. That would give her more leverage.

I want to try and help, but the more I dig for help, the more there is only so much I can do. I will visit him again towards Christmas, and bring him some goodies. CPS is the only option, did talk to my father in law, who was a former cop, now retired. You need proof, and not 2nd hand information. He says. The laws protect the criminals these days. He knows, and he's right.

My feeling on all this, Joe ruined that family, he did. I'm glad he's gone, he was a POS. Always was. I told Mary one time, I hope Joe never hurt you in any way. I know he antagonized her a lot. She never answered me.....

I do want to talk to him, but I certainly don't want to upset him. Mary has tried to talk to him, and he gets upset when you bring too much up. My question, when did the lines become so blurred with him that he accepted all this? I don't know. Only he can answer that. Mary sounds beat, as if she has given up. If I was her, I wouldn't give up. She is going to have one hell of a holy mess on her hands once he does pass away. I could see Joes wife wanting to stay there, but the taxes alone, she wouldn't be able to afford it. She's got her sugar daddy right now. Mr. Reynold also does estate planning, lets hope his estate, and his will is secure when he does go. Just sad. It begs the question, if you knew then, what you know now, would you, and could you change a situation. Life happens, but damn.......
